planting.note: Fall-sow cleaned seed or set container plants into well-drained soil; it tolerates both sun and the shade of taller thornscrub companions.

directions: Desert yaupon is a stiff, intricately branched shrub of the thornscrub understory, unrelated to true yaupon holly despite the shared common name, with light gray twigs and small spine-tipped leaves. Bright red berries on female plants persist through winter and are an important cold-season food source for brush-country birds. It is one of the more shade-tolerant thornscrub shrubs, thriving as an understory layer beneath guajillo, blackbrush, or granjeno as well as in open sun. Give it well-drained soil and infrequent watering, and let it fill in naturally as a dense low thicket.
sources: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department Ecological Mapping Systems
